# Gaṇeśa, spelled the way the sources wrote it
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Gaṇeśa** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Gaṇeśa's myths are among the most beloved in South Asia, weaving together domestic drama, divine error, and comic redemption. He is the son of Pārvatī — and, by adoption or blood, of Śiva — and his stories revolve around the tensions of belonging, authority, and transformation. In the best-known account, Pārvatī fashions a boy from turmeric paste (haridrā) to guard her door while she bathes.  When Śiva returns and is refused entry, he strikes off the boy's head in rage.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Gaṇeśa
- **ASCII form:** ganesha
- **Meaning:** "Lord of the gaṇas (from गणेश)"
- **Domain of influence:** Wisdom, Beginnings, Obstacle-Removal
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** गणेश
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 84 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Gaṇeśa** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *ganesha* and **Gaṇeśa** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Gaṇeśa** lives at [/sites/ganesha/](/sites/ganesha/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ganesha/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ganesha/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ganesha/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Gaṇeśa** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Education, Research & Knowledge** — Wisdom and learning; students invoke him before every exam.
- **Writing, Publishing & Media** — The scribe of the Mahābhārata; he broke his own tusk rather than let Vyāsa's dictation stop.
- **Startups & Venture Creation** — Lord of beginnings and remover of obstacles; every Indian venture opens with him.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
